title: Global allocator configuration, limits, mutex, and method-table state representations

scope.rationale: These are the complete private mem0 identities and the Sqlite3Config identities directly read by the admitted global allocation core. They consolidate into the process-lifetime Manager owner.
excluded_responsibilities: Public sqlite3_mem_methods ABI layout, which is generated separately
Sqlite3Config fields unrelated to allocator or static page-cache initialization

external_source_responsibilities: Pinned default SQLITE_MAX_MEMORY value and writable-static-data profile
Configured allocator method callback validity and initialization lifecycle
dependencies.caller_closure: All global configuration, limit, nearly-full, mutex, method-table, and status storage read or written by the six-function global allocator core is represented.

inputs: Pinned profile defaults and pre-initialization allocator configuration
outputs: One process-lifetime allocator owner with backend callbacks, status enablement, limits, nearly-full state, mutex, and static page-cache configuration
contracts.ownership: Manager owns copied backend callback transport and process-lifetime status/limit state; backend context ownership remains with its configurator.
contracts.state_and_results: Default hard/soft limits are zero, memory status is enabled, and callback state is initialized before sqlite3Malloc-family calls.
contracts.locks_callbacks_io: Manager.lock represents mem0.mutex. Backend represents sqlite3GlobalConfig.m. No I/O.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: Representation carries failed backend initialization without partial started state; sequencing behavior is separately assigned.

representation_differences: C mem0 and the allocator-relevant subset of sqlite3Config are consolidated into one Manager.
SQLITE_MAX_MEMORY is zero in the pinned profile and is represented by Manager.hard_limit defaulting to zero.
The C sqlite3_mem_methods object is normalized to Backend callbacks after configuration; MethodsBackend preserves the public ABI transport.
Writable-static-data indirection is absent in the pinned profile; both C macros resolve to direct process globals.

oracle.protocol: Infrastructure C/Zig differentials compare configured backend lifecycle/copies, memory-status behavior, limits, nearly-full effects, statistics, shutdown, and shuffled reinitialization. Native tests inspect default and transition state.
internal_observations: valid and invalid static page-cache configuration state
oracle.normalization: Private C and Zig global addresses and aggregate field offsets may differ; callback event order and all state values are exact.

assurance.oom: No representation allocation; backend initialization failure leaves started false.
assurance.io_crash_concurrency: No I/O. Manager mutex protects allocator/status state, but source mutex subsystem integration remains open.
assurance.malformed_input: Invalid callback/configuration inputs belong to configuration behavior.
assurance.continuation: Manager can stop and restart while retaining source-corresponding process status ownership.
assurance.performance: Private state consolidation removes indirection; callback invocation remains direct.

integration.native_call_path: db_allocator heap fallback reaches ensureProcessManager; public memory APIs route through the same process owner.
integration.bounded_owner_retired: Allocator-specific status scalar fields were retired in favor of source-corresponding ten-slot arrays.

independent_review.notes: Must verify default profile values, state consolidation, callback lifetime, and initialization/mutex boundaries.

known_blockers: Configuration/init/shutdown behavior is not part of this representation unit.
Final mutex subsystem ownership and independent review remain open.

implementation_spans: upstream/sqlite/src/malloc.c:36-57 was reviewed for SQLITE_MAX_MEMORY, complete Mem0Global storage, process initializer, and WSD alias
upstream/sqlite/src/sqliteInt.h:1290-1312 and 4280-4315 were reviewed for direct sqlite3GlobalConfig selection and the complete allocator/page-cache-relevant Sqlite3Config field neighborhood
upstream/sqlite/src/global.c:230-300 was reviewed through the sqlite3Config singleton initializer and selected default values
src/core/memory.zig Manager/process_manager fields are the canonical AST-hashed consolidated representation; global-status-primitives owns the embedded ten-slot status dependency
callers: malloc.c:63/95-222 consumes mem0 mutex, soft/hard limits, nearlyFull, allocator init/end, and static page-cache validation
malloc.c:246-305 mallocWithAlarm/sqlite3Malloc, 344-402 size/free, and 503-552 realloc consume bMemstat, backend methods, limits, mutex, and status state
main.c:301-302 passes pPage/szPage/nPage to PCache setup; main.c:500-531 configures allocator methods, memstatus, and static page cache before initialization
global-allocator-core-for-connection-growth owns the six allocation functions; configuration/init/shutdown and public heap-limit functions are separate behavior units
callees: Representation fields have no callees; sqlite3_mem_methods callbacks and context are configurator-owned and invoked by allocator behavior units
Direct WSD macros select sqlite3Config/mem0 because SQLITE_OMIT_WSD is absent; SQLITE_MAX_MEMORY defaults to zero
Manager consolidates mem0 and the allocator subset of Sqlite3Config while preserving callback values and process lifetime rather than C aggregate layout
assertions_branches_cleanup: No behavioral blocks belong to representation declarations; selected defaults are bMemstat=true, soft/hard limits zero, nearlyFull=false, allocator callbacks zero before initialization, pPage=null, szPage=0, and profile nPage default
Static page-cache validity branches and backend initialization rollback are behavior owned by global allocator init/shutdown, not credited here
No representation allocation, lock action, callback, I/O, cleanup, or failure transition occurs until a behavior owner consumes the state
upstream_tests: upstream/sqlite/test/memsubsys1.test and memsubsys2.test observe memstatus, allocator statistics, and page-cache configuration consequences
upstream/sqlite/test/malloc.test, malloc2.test, malloc3.test, and malloc5.test exercise configured/default allocator state, limits, OOM, and continuation
upstream/sqlite/test/pcache2.test observes static page-cache status consumers; configuration misuse timing is covered by config tests
Project memory.zig state/default tests and infrastructure differential inspect consolidated state but are not durable promotion receipts
